scenario_name: Agent loses track of card replace after fraud investigation and card upgrade tangent
judge_summary: The assistant handled the core banking tasks effectively: it locked the card, surfaced transaction details, filed fraud reports, and completed the replacement card order, while also giving a solid rewards-card comparison. However, it failed to promptly adjust when the user redirected the conversation to the Amazon charge and later disregarded the user’s preference about Apple Pay, indicating weaknesses in repair behavior and short-term contextual tracking. Overall, it was useful and clear but showed rigidity when the user tried to change course mid-flow.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the card, investigated and reported fraudulent charges, and confirmed placement of the replacement card order with the user’s requested shipping, which were the user’s main goals.

criteria.criterion: Before locking the lost card, the agent asks whether the customer wants it locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “Would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821 now?” and the user replies, “Yes, please go ahead and lock it,” before the ledger shows tool: lock_card() being called.

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay)
criteria.reasoning: The bot explicitly asks, “Would you like to add your new River Visa ending 4821 to Apple Pay or Google Pay so you can use it while the replacement card is on its way?” (repeated multiple times).

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: After the user specifies shipping and asks to confirm the order, the bot clarifies, “Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with standard shipping?” and the user answers, “Yes, please place the order with standard shipping…,” before process_card_replacement() is called.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: Following process_card_replacement() with order summary containing “Order ID: RPL-2026-001843,” the bot tells the user, “Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” matching the tool result.

criteria.criterion: When the customer asks to upgrade or switch to the Summit card, the agent declines honestly — explaining it cannot process an upgrade and can only recommend cards — rather than treating it as replacing the Summit card instead of River
criteria.reasoning: When asked “Can you switch me to the Summit card from here, or can you only recommend it?”, the bot answers, “I can only recommend cards here — I can’t switch you to Summit Rewards or process an upgrade/application in this chat,” clearly declining the upgrade capability.

criteria.criterion: After the Summit upgrade is declined, the agent continues the existing River Visa replacement from where it left off, rather than starting a brand-new replacement request
criteria.reasoning: Immediately after declining the Summit upgrade, the bot resumes with “We can still finish replacing your lost River Visa ending 4821 now. Which shipping would you like…,” and later records_shipping_type and then calls process_card_replacement for the same card, continuing the existing flow rather than initiating a new one.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: Content-wise the bot provided detailed transaction info, correctly filed fraud reports, explained the Summit card comparison, and clearly confirmed replacement card details, though it unnecessarily initiated Apple Pay provisioning after the user explicitly declined it.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: The assistant ignored three consecutive user clarifications about wanting the Amazon charge investigated before pushing mobile wallet options, only correcting course after repeated pushes, and later had to walk back the Apple Pay action after the user said they did not want it.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant generally tracked state (fraud reports, replacement order, card comparison) but showed a notable lapse by repeatedly asking about Apple/Google Pay after the user shifted intent to the Amazon charge and then auto-adding the card to Apple Pay despite a later explicit preference against it.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was consistently clear, polite, and professional, with concise explanations and appropriate reassurance especially around fraud and card replacement.
